The columns, name variants and sheet patterns the workbook parser reads

Source: R/fiss_parse.R
knw_fiss_columns.Rd

The provincial Fish Data Submission workbook has four step sheets: Step 1 (reference and location), Step 2 (fish collection: effort and the catch per species), Step 3 (individual fish) and Step 4 (stream site). Its editions name the sheets and some columns differently. This returns what knw_fiss_parse_step() reads, so a caller can see it without reading the code.

Usage

knw_fiss_columns()

Value

A list: wanted, the columns read per step (plus keys, read on every step), in janitor::make_clean_names() form; variants, a named character vector mapping an edition's column name to the canonical one; step_pattern, the regular expression that finds each step's sheet by its lower-cased name.

Examples

cols <- knw_fiss_columns()
cols$step_pattern
#>                                           step1_ref_loc 
#>                             "step.?1|ref.*loc|location" 
#>                                         step2_fish_coll 
#>                   "step.?2|fish.?coll|collection.?form" 
#>                                        step3_indiv_fish 
#>                                         "step.?3|indiv" 
#>                                         step4_site_data 
#> "step.?4|stream.?site|site.?data|site.?card|site.?coll" 
# the pre-2012 edition's names and the ones they are read as
cols$variants
#>          gazetted_names        alias_local_name waterbody_id_identifier 
#>         "gazetted_name"            "local_name"          "waterbody_id" 
#>            species_code                  method            haul_or_pass 
#>               "species"       "sampling_method"             "haul_pass" 
#> haul_number_pass_number        date_yyyy_mm_day 
#>             "haul_pass"           "survey_date"
